construct: the OPEN listbox as an out-of-flow overlay - `position: absolute; top: 34px` under a `position: relative` trigger, so the popover does not participate in the trigger's flow
why: 'Overlays rather than reflows' is the one structural fact that separates a combobox from an accordion, and it is carried entirely by the popover being out of flow. The `top: 34px` inset is what places it just under the trigger; if the inset is lost the list lands ON the trigger, and if the out-of-flow-ness is lost the trigger grows to contain the list. Both failures are recognisable at a glance and neither is a colour.

canvas.note: layoutPositioning ABSOLUTE with a y offset under the trigger

mustHave: the popover appears BELOW the trigger, not on top of it and not inside it
the trigger's own height is unchanged by the popover's presence - the trigger is one text line tall
the popover's left edge lines up with the trigger's left edge
the popover lists both options, stacked vertically

predictedWall.why: core/emit-figma-script.ts:6536 (and :6609, :7382) degrades with exactly this code and the message 'the out-of-flow placement was refused (parent not auto-layout); the child stayed in flow'. 'The child stayed in flow' IS the combobox failure mode this case exists to catch: a popover that reflows the trigger instead of overlaying it. The trigger here is a flex row, so the parent SHOULD be auto-layout and the refusal should not fire - which is why this is `hard` rather than `expected-wall`. If it fires anyway, the message names the cause precisely.
